newsitem.title: FRANCE: Axa/UAP deal adds fizz to French bank stocks.
newsitem.headline: Axa/UAP deal adds fizz to French bank stocks.

text.p: French bank stocks took on new life on Wednesday as news of the mega-merger between insurers Axa and UAP revived interest in financial stocks and the prospects for further restructuring, traders and analysts said.

Shares in Credit Commercial de France (CCF) surged more than three percent against the market trend and traders said the bank was back under the spotlight as a more plausible takeover target than bigger rivals BNP and Societe Generale.
"I suppose people see CCF as a possible target mainly because of its size and because it would be a lot cheaper in absolute terms," said one trader.
The stock was up 3.53 percent at 252.3 francs at 1325 GMT after earlier hitting a day high of 254 francs.
Societe Generale too gained from a turn to more positive sentiment, rising more than two percent and stood at 578 francs, up 1.94 percent at 1327 GMT.
"Societe Generale has been a big underperformer, there seems to be a big push to financials," said one analyst.
"Societe was one of the laggards yesterday, the Axa/UAP deal is good news for financials generally," said a trader.
BNP, another large player beside SocGen, fell heavily in what traders said was natural consolidation after a large rise on Tuesday on the back of the Axa/UAP merger news.
BNP owns 17.5 percent of Axa. According to Axa and UAP, BNP could hold 6.5 percent of the merged insurance group and 5.9 percent of the voting rights.
The stock was down 2.63 percent at 211.1 francs at 1331 GMT although off a day low of 210.1 francs.
"BNP was up 8.5 percent yesterday," said one trader. "It's basically consolidation.
Another described yesterday's surge in BNP as "madness".
Paribas stock too gained strongly, up 1.92 percent at 349.6 francs 1341 GMT after hitting a year high of 350.9 franc earlier.
French bank stocks have long been suffering from poor investment sentiment due to a depressed French banking climate and relative lack of competitivity versus their international rivals.
